question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can appreciate by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사절 안에서 주어인 an attachment가 '보여지는' 수동의 관계이므로, 과거분사 'shown'이 be동사 뒤에 보어로 쓰인 수동태 구조는 어법상 자연스럽습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사 Santa Fe를 부연 설명하는 관계부사 'where' 뒤에 주어(he)와 자동사(worked)로 구성된 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 올바른 쓰임입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어인 Houser's designs가 전통에 '뿌리를 두고 있다'는 수동의 의미를 나타내므로, 형용사처럼 쓰인 과거분사 'rooted'는 어법상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 등위접속사 but 뒤에 이어지는 절에서 주어인 'his sculpture'가 단수형이므로, 현재시제 단수 동사인 'transcends'는 수일치와 태 모두 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 대명사 'it'은 앞서 언급된 조각상인 'The sculpture Reverie'를 가리킵니다. 따라서 조각상이 스스로를 감상하는 주체가 아니라 사람들에 의해 '감상되는' 대상이므로 수동의 관계가 성립되어야 합니다. 능동형인 'can appreciate'는 목적어도 없을 뿐만 아니라 문맥상 의미가 통하지 않으므로 수동태인 'can be appreciated'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (E) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 주어와 동사의 행위 관계 및 목적어 존재 여부로 판정
(B) 관계부사 — 뒤에 완전한 절이 오며 장소 선행사를 수식하는 구조 확인
(C) 분사의 형용사 역할 — 주어가 감정을 느끼거나 상태에 놓이는 수동 관계 분석
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is __(A) shown__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(B) where__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(C) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture __(D) transcends__ race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it __(E) can appreciate__ by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 of의 목적어로 준동사인 동명사가 쓰였으며, 주어인 We가 '홀로 남겨지는' 대상이 되므로 수동태 동명사인 being left는 어법상 자연스럽습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주어인 we가 고요함과 타인의 부재에 의해 '충격을 받는(struck)' 수동의 대상이므로, 분사구문의 수동태를 이끄는 과거분사 struck은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 선행사 other people을 수식하며 관계절 안에서 주어 역할을 수행하는 주격 관계대명사 who는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 동명사구인 Reading a book collaboratively가 문장의 주어이므로, 단수 동사 is로 일치시킨 수일치는 완전하게 맞습니다.

question.explanation: (D) "which"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "in which"로 고쳐야 한다. 문장의 골격을 분석해보면, Consider로 시작하는 명령문에서 joining이 목적어이고 a reading group이 동명사의 목적어입니다. 이를 수식하는 관계절 내부를 보면, 주어 everybody, 동사 takes turns, 동사의 목적어 역할을 하는 분사구 reading aloud가 모두 갖춰진 완전한 구조를 이루고 있습니다. 관계대명사 which는 관계절 내부에서 대명사(주어, 목적어, 보어 중 하나) 역할을 해야 하므로 뒤에 불완전한 절이 이어져야 하지만, 여기서는 빠진 격이 없는 완벽한 절이 왔기 때문에 which는 비문입니다. 지문의 문맥상 '그 독서 모임 안에서(in the group)'라는 부사적 의미를 포함해야 하므로, 전치사를 보충하여 in which로 고치거나 관계부사 where로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 따라서 정답은 (D)입니다.
keyPoints: (D) 관계대명사 vs 전치사+관계대명사 — 뒤따르는 절의 완전성 여부로 판정
(B) 분사구문 능동 vs 수동 — 의미상 주어와의 능동·수동 관계 파악
(E) 주어-동사 수일치 — 동명사구가 주어일 때 단수 취급
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being__ left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly __(B) struck__ by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(C) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group __(D) which__ everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively __(E) is__ a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page)

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are something useful produced by a mind.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주어인 'A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony'가 'A and B' 형태로 연결된 복수 주어이므로 복수 정동사인 'are'는 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): -thing으로 끝나는 대명사(something)를 뒤에서 수식하는 구조이며, 정신에 의해 '만들어진' 대상이라는 수동의 의미를 나타내므로 과거분사 'produced'는 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 동명사 수식구 또는 명사구 'The literary rendering (of the original novel)'에서 주어의 핵은 단수 명사인 'rendering'이므로 단수 정동사인 'is'는 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어 'Both' 뒤에서 타동사 'influence'와 목적어 'audiences'로 이루어진 완전한 문장 성분 뒤에 위치하여, 동사인 'influence'를 수식하므로 부사 'powerfully'의 사용은 어법상 옳습니다.

question.explanation: If절 내에서 'a thousand lines of letters in UNIX'가 주어 역할을 하고 있습니다. 접속사 If가 이끄는 부사절이 성립하기 위해서는 절 내에 정동사(finite verb)가 반드시 존재해야 합니다. 하지만 (A)의 'qualifying'은 준동사인 현재분사로, 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어 해당 절에 정동사가 존재하지 않는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 준동사인 'qualifying'을 3인칭 단수 정동사인 'qualifies'(또는 복수 주어 'lines'에 일치시킨 'qualify')로 고쳐야 부사절의 어법적 뼈대가 올바르게 완성됩니다. 주어 내부의 수식 관계에 현혹되어 문장 전체의 정동사 자리를 놓치지 않아야 합니다.
keyPoints: (A) 정·준동사 — 부사절 내 정동사의 유무로 판정
(B) 수일치 — coordinate conj. 'and'로 연결된 복수 주어 판정
(C) 분사능수동 — 피수식어 something과의 수동 관계 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(A) qualifying__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, __(B) are__ in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(C) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel __(D) is__ as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences __(E) powerfully__. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): kept는 과거의 역사적 사실(사바나에서 살았을 때)을 기술하므로 과거시제 동사 kept는 어법상 자연스럽습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 명령문 train의 주어는 생략된 주어인 you이므로, 목적어 자리에 주어와 동일 대상을 가리키는 재귀대명사 yourself를 쓴 것은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 계획표나 일기에 '잘 진행되었던 일'을 적는 것이므로 과거 일어난 상황을 진술하는 정동사 went는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 주어인 reality가 3인칭 단수이므로, 이에 호응하는 현재형 단수 동사 follows는 수일치상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: (A) "what"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "that"로 고쳐야 한다. 본문에서 대시(-) 뒤의 'a trait'는 동격명사구의 핵심어(선행사) 역할을 합니다. 이 선행사에 걸리는 두 개의 주격 관계대명사절이 등위접속사 but으로 병렬 구성되어 있습니다. 즉, 'that kept us alive ~'와 'that can prevent happiness ~'가 병렬되어야 하므로, 선행사 'a trait'가 존재하는 한 관계대명사는 선행사를 포함한 관계사인 what이 될 수 없습니다. 따라서 학생들에게 보인 틀린 표현인 'what'을, 선행사를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사인 'that'(또는 which)으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바른 구조가 됩니다.
keyPoints: (A) 관계사 — 선행사 유무에 따른 that과 what의 선택
(C) 대명사 — 명령문 주어(you)와 일치하는 재귀대명사의 사용
(E) 수일치 — 단수 주어에 부합하는 정동사의 단수형 수일치 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait __(A) what__ __(B) kept__ us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train __(C) yourself__ to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what __(D) went__ well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality __(E) follows__. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We reconstruct memories rather than retrieved the video from memory.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 선행사인 'shapes, colors, and concepts'를 수식하며 관계절 내에서 learned의 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사 'that'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 전치사구 'rather than' 뒤에서 동명사구의 머리 역할을 하거나 앞의 'to store~' 구조와 비교를 나타내는 'storing'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어 'People'을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로서, 뒤에 동사 'lack'과 'remember'를 이끌며 선행사와의 관계를 자연스럽게 이어주므로 'who'는 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 동명사구 주어 'representing the world as abstract ideas and features'는 단수 취급하므로 단수 동사 'comes'는 수일치상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: (B) "retrieved"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "retrieving"로 고쳐야 한다. 이 문장은 원문에서 'rather than'을 통해 'reconstruct memories'와 'retrieving the video'라는 두 대조적 행위를 연결하고 있습니다. 'rather than' 뒤에 준동사가 연결될 때, 앞의 동사구인 'reconstruct memories'에 맞추어 동사원형 'retrieve'를 쓰거나, 병렬 구조 및 전치사의 목적어로서 동명사 'retrieving'을 사용해야 합니다. 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 'the video'를 직접 취할 수 없는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 'retrieved'를 'retrieving'이나 'retrieve'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (B) 병렬 구조 — 대조 관계에 있는 동사/준동사의 형태 일치 및 뒤따르는 목적어 유무 판정
(E) 주어-동사 수일치 — 동명사구 주어 뒤의 동사 수일치 판정
(A) 관계대명사의 격 — 관계절 내에서 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장을 이끄는 관계사 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts __(A) that__ we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than __(B) retrieved__ the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than __(C) storing__ a raw bitmap image file. People __(D) who__ lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features __(E) comes__ at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity?

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not to seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity?

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 동명사구 'making time for exercise'가 문장의 주어 역할을 하고 있으므로 주어 자리에 쓰인 동명사 making은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 관계부사 where가 이끄는 절 안에서 진짜 주어 핵(head)은 단수 명사인 'the beauty'이므로, 단수 동사인 comes로 수일치한 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 부사 purely의 수식을 받으며, 뒤에 오는 명사 activities를 앞에서 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 obligatory는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 시간을 나타내는 부사절 접속사 as가 이끄는 절에서 주어인 you에 호응하여 절을 완결하는 정동사(finite verb) 자리이므로 현재시제 동사인 wait은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 제안이나 권유의 의미를 나타내는 표현인 'why not' 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 이어져야 합니다. 이 문장은 'rather than viewing ~'이라는 부사구 뒤에 'why not'이 연결되어 청자에게 제안하는 구조를 취하고 있습니다. 따라서 to-부정사의 형태인 'to seize'는 비문이며, 동사원형인 seize로 고쳐야 합니다. many 혹은 chores 등의 긴 수식어구에 현혹되어 'why not'의 고유한 통사적 특징을 간과하기 쉽습니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 제안 표현 'why not' 뒤 동사원형 판정
(B) 주어-동사 수일치 — 수식어가 길게 붙은 주어의 핵심 명사 찾기
(C) 형용사 vs 부사 — 명사를 수식하는 형용사 수식 관계 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, __(A) making__ time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores __(B) comes__ into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely __(C) obligatory__ activities, why not __(D) to seize__ these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you __(E) wait__ for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): that절의 주어 핵인 a source가 단수형이므로 단수 동사 has를 쓴 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 뒤에 주어(it)와 동사(was)를 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지므로 접속사인 while을 쓴 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어인 Your auditory areas가 뒤따르는 목적어(its continuation)를 능동적으로 예측하고 있다는 의미이므로 현재분사 predicting은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어인 people이 무언가 자신들을 깨웠다고 '주장하면서' 경찰에 전화했다는 능동의 관계를 나타내므로 현재분사 claiming은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: (D) "stopping"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "stopped"로 고쳐야 한다. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains 라는 부사절에서 접속사 after 뒤에 주어 New York City가 오고 그 뒤를 잇는 정동사가 필요합니다. 하지만 제시된 stopping은 준동사이므로 이 절의 동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 따라서 이 문맥에서 과거 시제의 정동사인 stopped로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 부사절 내의 주어 뒤에는 정동사가 위치해야 함
(A) 명사구 수일치 — 전치사구의 수식을 받는 명사구 주어의 핵과 동사의 수일치
(C) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 목적어를 취하는 타동사의 진행형 능동 분사 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, __(A) has__ just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound __(B) while__ it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were __(C) predicting__ its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City __(D) stopping__ running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night __(E) claiming__ that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: While doing the laundry, just do the laundry

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 to의 목적어 자리에 이끄는 명사절 속에서, doing의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장 구조를 명사절로 만들어 주는 관계대명사 'what you're doing'은 어법상 올바른 쓰임입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 접속사 While 뒤에 주어와 be동사(you are)가 생략된 분사구문 형태인 'doing'은, 주어와의 관계가 능동이므로 현재분사 형태가 오는 것이 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 전치사 with 뒤에 목적어(your phone)와 목적격 보어 역할을 하는 분사가 오는 구조로, 전화기는 귀에 '대어지는(눌려지는)' 수동의 대상이므로 과거분사 'pressed'를 사용하는 것이 어법상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 주어인 3인칭 단수 명사구 'The same'에 맞추어 단수 동사형인 'applies'를 쓴 수일치 구조로 어법상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: (C) "did"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "would"로 고쳐야 한다. 본 문장에서 than 이하의 절은 실제 그렇게 행해질 가상의 상황을 비유하는 비교 구문으로, 주절의 'It doesn't take up...'과 비교하여 '만일 귀에 전화기를 대고 빨래를 한다면 걸릴 법한(가정/추측) 시간'을 뜻합니다. 따라서 did를 원래의 조동사 형태인 would로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (C) 가정한 상황의 조동사 — 가상의 상황에 상응하는 조동사 would 판단하기
(A) 관계대명사 vs 접속사 — 선행사가 없고 목적어가 빠진 자리에 명사절을 이끄는 what 검토
(D) 분사구부대상황 — with + 목적어 + 분사 구조에서 목적어와 분사의 수동 관계 파악
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to __(A) what you're doing__ at the moment no matter what it is. While __(B) doing__ the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it __(C) did__ when done with your phone __(D) pressed__ to your ear. The same __(E) applies__ to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 선행사인 단수 명사 'a critical factor'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에 오는 동사이므로, 단수형 동사인 determines를 쓴 것은 수일치상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 앞에 있는 선행사 'the leopard seal'을 수식하며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장이 이어지므로 주격 관계대명사인 which를 계속적 용법으로 쓴 것은 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 문장의 주어 'The penguins' solution'에 대해 주어를 보충 설명해 주는 주격 보어 자리이므로 명사적 용법의 to부정사인 to play는 어법상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어인 'One penguin's destiny'가 3인칭 단수이므로, 이에 호응하는 단수 동사의 형태 alters를 쓴 것은 수일치상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장의 전체 구조를 보면 '~하자마자'라는 뜻의 접속사 역할을 하는 명사구 'The moment (that) occurs'가 부사절 역할을 이끌고 있습니다. 따라서 뒤이어 문장의 진짜 주어인 'the rest of the penguins'에 호응하는 정동사(finite verb)가 나와야 합니다. 하지만 준동사인 watching은 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어 문장 전체에 본동사가 없는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 watching을 주절의 정동사이자 'the rest of the penguins(복수)'에 수일치시킨 복수형 현재 시제 동사인 watch로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정·준동사 — 부사절과 주절의 구조를 파악하여 본동사 자리인지 준동사 자리인지 판정
(A) 수일치 — 관계대명사절 내의 동사 수일치는 선행사의 단수/복수 여부에 일치
(B) 관계사 — 선행사의 종류와 뒷문장의 구성 성분 탈락 여부를 파악하여 주격 관계대명사 사용
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor that __(A) determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, __(B) which__ likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is __(C) to play__ the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins __(D) watching__ with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny __(E) alters__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에서 선행사인 단수 명사 the distance에 수일치하여 단수 현재완료형 동사인 has formed를 쓴 것은 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주절(We call template...) 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문으로, 주어인 we가 능동적으로 바라는 주체이므로 현재분사 hoping을 쓴 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어인 relationships(관계)는 유지되는 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 나타내는 'be + p.p.' 형태인 aren't kept로 쓰인 수동태 표현은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 가주어 it에 대응하는 진주어 자리로, 부정사구의 부정형인 'not to-v' 형태에 맞추어 to let을 쓴 것은 어법상 옳습니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 뼈대를 살펴보면, 조동사 shouldn't 뒤에 동사원형 bother가 위치하고 있으며, '일부러 ~하다', '~하는 것을 귀찮아하다'라는 의미로 동사 bother 뒤에는 목적어로 동명사(v-ing) 또는 to-부정사(to-v)가 와야 합니다. 따라서 대상을 능동적으로 부르는 맥락이므로 과거분사나 과거동사 형태인 called는 이 자리에 올 수 없으며, calling(또는 to call)으로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정·준동사 — 동사 bother의 목적으로 쓰이는 준동사 형태 판정
(B) 분사능수동 — 주절의 주어가 행동을 직접 하는 주체일 때 현재분사 사용
(E) to-v/v-ing — 가주어 it에 대한 진주어 역할을 이끄는 to-부정사구
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that __(A) has formed__ and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, __(B) hoping__ that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.
